diagram_candidates.claim: The corner path has distinct one-sided tangents and a centered chord in neither tangent direction, while the cusp path has coincident samples at ±h, zero centered chord, and zero derivative at 0.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source introduces two explicit planar paths to demonstrate geometric hypotheses used by a string method. A paired sketch can make the corner tangent mismatch and cusp chord degeneracy immediately visible.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Panel 1: draw R_c(s)=(s,0) for s≤0 and R_c(s)=(0,s) for s≥0, mark the origin, one-sided tangent arrows (1,0) and (0,1), sample points R_c(−h), R_c(h), and the centered chord (h,h). Panel 2: draw R_u(s)=(s²,0), mark the coincident samples R_u(−h)=R_u(h)=(h²,0), the zero centered chord, and R_u'(0)=0. Keep arrows and labels consistent with the exact coordinate formulas.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The formulas and geometric consequences are explicit in the source; the proof confirms the derivatives and chord computations. No current defect or proof dependence on a diagram was found; this is an optional explanation.
